title: OCR bounding-box arithmetic can overflow
summary: The Mistral OCR adapter parses remote OCR image bounding boxes and normalizes object-style `x`/`y`/`w`/`h` coordinates with unchecked signed addition. A response-controlled `x = i64::MAX, w = 1` or `y = i64::MAX, h = 1` panics in overflow-checked builds and can wrap into inverted extracted-image metadata in optimized builds with overflow checks disabled.

codeEvidence.label: Remote OCR JSON is parsed into the adapter
codeEvidence.code:
let value: Value = ureq::post(&format!("{}/v1/ocr", self.base_url()))
    .set("Authorization", &format!("Bearer {api_key}"))
    .set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .send_json(ocr_request_body(
        &request.media_type,
        &bytes,
        model_pin,
        pages.as_deref(),
    ))
    .map_err(http_error)?
    .into_json()
    .map_err(|err| AdapterError::ContractViolation(err.to_string()))?;
parse_ocr_response(value, model_pin)
codeEvidence.explanation: After an approved OCR call, the remote service controls the JSON `value` passed into `parse_ocr_response()`.

codeEvidence.label: Response pages are mapped through page parsing
codeEvidence.code:
fn parse_ocr_response(value: Value, model_pin: &str) -> Result<OcrResponse> {
    let pages = value
        .get("pages")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .ok_or_else(|| AdapterError::ContractViolation("OCR response missing pages".to_owned()))?
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(fallback_index, page)| parse_ocr_page(page, fallback_index))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
codeEvidence.explanation: `parse_ocr_response()` performs a shape check for the `pages` array, then forwards each remote page toward image parsing.

codeEvidence.label: Image parser forwards remote bbox data
codeEvidence.code:
fn parse_ocr_image(value: &Value) -> Result<OcrImage> {
    let raw_base64 = value
        .get("image_base64")
        .or_else(|| value.get("base64"))
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let (media_type, data) = split_data_uri(raw_base64);
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
        .decode(data)
        .map_err(|err| AdapterError::ContractViolation(err.to_string()))?;
    Ok(OcrImage {
        bytes,
        media_type: value
            .get("media_type")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or(media_type)
            .to_owned(),
        bbox: parse_bbox(value.get("bbox").unwrap_or(value)),
codeEvidence.explanation: The remote image object controls either the nested `bbox` field or, if absent, the top-level coordinate fields passed to `parse_bbox()`.

codeEvidence.label: Width and height are added without overflow checks
codeEvidence.explanation: `x1`, `y1`, `w`, and `h` are response-controlled `i64` values. The object-form fallback computes `x1 + w` and `y1 + h` without `checked_add()` or a geometry predicate.

codeEvidence.label: Parsed boxes are serialized into extracted-image metadata
codeEvidence.explanation: When optimized builds wrap instead of panicking, the resulting impossible `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` tuple is preserved as image metadata.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that remote OCR coordinates must be proven safe and geometrically valid before KCS derives `x2` and `y2`. `parse_bbox()` accepts object-style start-plus-extent coordinates and evaluates `x1 + w` and `y1 + h` directly on response-controlled `i64` values, then returns the tuple without checking for overflow, negative extents, or inverted boxes.

validation.method: static source trace plus local synthetic arithmetic probe
validation.summary: The source trace confirms that OCR response JSON controls the image `bbox` fields and that object-style `w` and `h` operands reach unchecked signed addition. The local PoC confirms the two relevant build outcomes: overflow-checked builds panic, while an optimized build with overflow checks disabled wraps into an inverted coordinate.
assertions: `serde_json::Value::as_i64()` constrains type but not arithmetic range.
`x1 + w` and `y1 + h` are evaluated before any geometry validation.
The array form returns four values directly and is not the overflow trigger, although it still needs geometry validation.
limitations: No live OCR endpoint was contacted.
No end-to-end downstream consumer of wrapped metadata was exercised.
Batch-wide recovery after a panic was not measured.

attackPath.summary: A remote OCR response actor answers an approved OCR request with an image object whose `bbox` uses `x`/`y` plus `w`/`h` values near `i64` boundaries. KCS computes the derived edges without checked arithmetic, causing a panic or wrapped metadata depending on overflow-check configuration.

dataflow.outcome: active OCR operation panic or wrapped inverted metadata

reachability.summary: The attacker must influence the response to an OCR request that KCS has already approved; there is no inbound KCS listener involved in this path.
reachability.attacker: remote OCR service, compatible configured OCR endpoint, or actor able to influence that response
preconditions: online OCR is enabled and an approved OCR request is sent
the response includes an image with object-style `bbox` coordinates using `w` or `h`
the chosen operands overflow signed 64-bit addition or produce invalid geometry
reachability.outcome: availability harm to OCR processing or invalid image coordinate metadata

impact.why: The response crosses a trust boundary and can reliably trigger panic or metadata-integrity failure, but the demonstrated effect is bounded to OCR processing and does not bypass authorization or disclose credentials.

likelihood.why: Once the remote response actor is in position, the operands are direct JSON fields with no arithmetic guard.

limitations: The array and explicit-corner forms avoid the overflowing addition.
The finding does not demonstrate arbitrary code execution, cross-scope persistence, or credential disclosure.

remediation.summary: Use checked arithmetic for start-plus-extent coordinates and reject negative, overflowing, inverted, or unreasonable bounding boxes before constructing `OcrImage` metadata.
recommendations: Replace `x1 + w` and `y1 + h` with `checked_add()` after rejecting negative `w` and `h`.
Apply a shared final predicate that enforces `x2 >= x1` and `y2 >= y1` for array, explicit-corner, and width/height forms.
Consider returning `Result<Option<[i64; 4]>>` so invalid coordinates can be reported as contract violations instead of being conflated with absent coordinates.
If page or image dimensions are available, reject coordinates outside those bounds.
regressionTests: Object-form `x = i64::MAX, w = 1` is rejected without panic.
Normal object-form `x = 10, y = 5, w = 20, h = 7` still returns `[10, 5, 30, 12]`.
Negative widths or heights are rejected.
Array and explicit-corner boxes with inverted geometry are rejected.
